native_simplicity.evidence: Selects one research/refinement campaign and avoids hydration, implementation, commit, or release side effects.

architectural_fit.evidence: Directly uses the p4 distinction between 3-tier product flow and 4-plane operating model.

governance_safety.evidence: Blocks public sync/release, public checkout mutation, cockpit/project writes, credentials, dependencies, kernel/governance/M1, commits, pushes, and destructive actions.

pm_orchestration_quality.evidence: Compares public update, four-plane language, backup/private remote, cockpit cleanup, packaging, and hydration alternatives.

iterative_quality.evidence: Uses one selected strategy plus a bounded three-child plan and one replay.

bounded_implementation.evidence: Next campaign remains research/refinement only and explicitly stops before ship_task or hydrate_task.

operator_ux.evidence: Ends with a concrete operator approval prompt and clear next-choice menu.

iteration_history.finding: Initial option board treated four-plane vocabulary and public update policy as separate top-level campaigns, which risked selecting a shallow documentation lane before the product boundary was resolved.
iteration_history.disposition: Recomposed selected lane to make four-plane vocabulary a sub-question of public-product update policy.

iteration_history.finding: Declaration now preserves protected boundaries and gives the operator an approval-ready next campaign.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Useful but too narrow; should be inside the public/update boundary strategy.
Important but protected and likely to involve private remote, backup, restore, or credential decisions.
Narrower UX cleanup and may require cockpit/project authority.
Operational packaging is useful but outside the approved no-commit campaign and not a product strategy lane.
Current PM mobility read reports zero safe hydration candidates.

residual_risks: Public freshness must be reverified with release-specific commands before any future public sync or release claim.
A future campaign must not mutate public azoth, cockpit, or project repos unless the operator explicitly approves that protected boundary.
The selected campaign should avoid converting strategy artifacts into canonical roadmap/backlog authority.
next_required_operator_decision: Approve or revise the selected next campaign declaration.
